To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the top-emitting MCLEDs exhibit efficiencies of 0.5-1.5% for light directly coupled into a 100-µm-diameter silica fibre and up to 14% when measured with an integrating sphere for a 62-degree collection angle.
top-emitting MCLEDs with a cavity size of 62 µm × 62 µm exhibit up to 14% external quantum efficiency and 0.5 % when coupled into a single mode fibre.

top-emitting InGaN/GaN microcavity light emitters have been fabricated, with efficiencies of up to 10%, which is the highest efficiency reported so far for top-emitting devices, and that a 0.5 % coupling efficiency has been achieved for light butt-coupled directly from the device into a 100 μm silica fiber.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication and characterization of high efficiency, top-emitting micro-cavity light-emitting devices.
the design and fabrication of top-emitting InP-based VCSELs and microcavity LEDs, with the ultimate objective of developing high-performance devices for optical interconnect applications.
the design, simulation, fabrication and characterization of top emitting microcavity light emitters, and the optimization of their performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given cavity design, the highest efficiencies are obtained when there is no detuning between the cavity mode and the spontaneous emission line.
the best results are obtained when the cavity mode is slightly red-shifted with respect to the spontaneous emission line, and the cavity length is in the 1.5-2 µm range.

the top-emitting micro-cavity light-emitting devices are a promising candidate for future high efficiency, low-cost and low-power consumption light sources for optical communications and optical storage systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the efficiency of the top-emitting MCLEDs can be increased by optimizing the design of the cavity.
the top-emitting InGAs/AlGaas microcavity light emitters have been successfully designed and fabricated, and their performance has been optimized.
we have demonstrated a top-emitting In0.2Ga0.8As/GaAs/Al0.25Ga0.75As microcavity LED with a 14% external quantum efficiency and 1.5% coupling into a 100-µm diameter fibre.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of top-emitting structures is a very promising route for the development of efficient, high-power MCLEDs.
the top-emitting MCLEDs have the same performance as bottom emitting ones, and can therefore be used for applications in the visible and infrared ranges.
the top-emitting MCLEDs can achieve high efficiency with a simple and inexpensive fabrication process.
